subject: Urban Planning
title: The Kowloon Walled City
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Kowloon Walled City.

hook.text: Kowloon Walled City housed 33,000 people in 6.5 acres — the densest place on Earth. No government controlled it.

buildup.text: A jurisdictional loophole left it ungoverned. Residents built upward — 14 stories high — with no building codes.

discovery.text: Inside: dentists, factories, temples, schools, and drug dens. It was a functioning city without any planning.

twist.text: Residents didn't want to leave. Despite the conditions, a tight-knit community had evolved over 40 years.

climax.text: It was demolished in 1994 and replaced by a park. Nothing else like it has existed before or since.

punchline.text: No planning. No government. 33,000 people made it work anyway.

quiz.question: What made Kowloon Walled City unique?
options: It was the first entirely solar-powered community in Asia
It was an ungoverned, self-built city with extreme density and no codes
It was designed by a famous architect as an experimental community
